simple.meaning: חָמַד (châmad) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to delight in.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 28 times across Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, Joshua, 2 Chronicles, and 7 more, beginning at Genesis 2:9. Its contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָמַד (H2530).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חָמַד (châmad) / H2530 is traced through Genesis 2:9, Genesis 3:6, Exodus 20:17, Exodus 34:24 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate. Then she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate it, too.
“You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
“You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
For I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your borders; neither shall any man desire your land when you go up to appear before Yahweh, your God, three times in the year.

“You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife. Neither shall you desire your neighbor’s house, his field, or his male servant, or his female servant, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor’s.”

You shall burn the engraved images of their gods with fire. You shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them, nor take it for yourself, lest you be snared in it; for it is an abomination to Yahweh your God.

When I saw among the plunder a beautiful Babylonian robe, two hundred shekels* A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces. of silver, and a wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels, then I coveted them and took them. Behold, they are hidden in the ground in the middle of my tent, with the silver under it.”

When Jehoshaphat and his people came to take their plunder, they found among them in abundance both riches and dead bodies, and precious jewels, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away. They took plunder for three days, it was so much.
“Because he knew no quietness within him,
Moreover your servant is warned by them.
“Hear my prayer, Yahweh, and give ear to my cry.
The chariots of God are tens of thousands and thousands of thousands.
“How long, you simple ones, will you love simplicity?
Don’t lust after her beauty in your heart,
The wicked desires the plunder of evil men,
There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise;
For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which you have desired,
Everyone who makes a carved image is vain.

definitions.full: H2530. chamad חָמַד verb desire, take pleasure in (Aramaic חֲמַד (not in Syriac); Arabic praise, eulogize, appove of ; Sabean חמדם in gratitude [praise] there-for DHM ZMG 1875, 595; 1876, 686 ) — Qal Perfect ׳ח Psa 68:17 ; Prov 12:12 ; חָֽמְדוּ 1:22 ; וְחָֽמְדוּ consecutive Micah 2:2 ; חֲמַדְתֶּם Isa 1:29 ; Imperfect יַחְמֹד Exod 34:24 ; 2 masculine singular תַּחְמֹד 20:16 (twice in verse) + 3t. (including Prov 6:25 jussive); suffix וָאֶחְמְדֵם Josh 7:21 ; וְנֶחְמְדֵ֫הוּ Isa 53:2 ; Passive participle חֲמוּדוֺ Psa 39:12 ; Job 20:20 , חֲמוּדֵיהֶם Isa 44:9 ; — desire: a. in bad sense of inordinate, ungoverned, selfish desire , followed by accusative Exod 20:17 (twice in verse) (E) = Deut 5:18 ( 5:18 b has תִּתְאַוֶּה ), Exod 34:24 (JE) Deut 7:25 ; Josh 7:21 (JE) Micah 2:2 ; Prov 12:12 ; of lustful desire 6:25 . b. = take pleasure in , of idolatrous tendency Isa 1:29 , so participle plural חֲמוּדֵיהֵם 44:9 their delightful things (things in which they delight, see also 44:11 and Bev JPhoenician xvii. 1888. p. 126 ); חָֽמְדוּ לָצוֺן לֵצִים Prov 1:22 how long do scorners delight in scoring. c. less often in good sense , said of God א חָמַד ׳הָהָר לְשִׁבְתּוֺ , poetic Psa 68:17 ; object the suffering servant of ׳י , Isa 53:2 no beauty in him, that we should desire him (choose him, be drawn toward him); passive participle collective חֲמוּדוֺ Psa 39:12 his desired things, i. e. chosen, choice, desirable (see Niph`al); so probably Job 20:20 . Niph`al Participle נֶחְמָד Gen 2:9 2 t.; הַנֶּחֱמָדִים Psa 19:11 ; — desirable: לְמַרְאֶה נ ׳עץ Gen 2:9 , ׳נ לְהַשְׂכִּיל 3:6 , ׳הַנֶּח מִזָּהָב Psa 19:11 which are more desirable than gold ; נֶחְמָד אוֺצָר Prov 21:20 desirable , i.e. costly treasure. Pi`el Perfect 1singular delight greatly ח ׳בְּצִלּוֺ וְיָשַׁ֫בְתִּי Song 2:3 in his shadow I greatly delighted and sate , i.e. sate with great delight. [ חֲמוּדָה ] noun feminine desirableness, preciousness — Plural absolute חֲמוּדוֺת Dan 9:23 ; חֲמוּדֹת Ezra 8:37; חֲמֻדוֺת 2Chr 20:25 4 t.; חֲמֻדֹת Gen 27:15 ; construct חֲמֻדוֺת Dan 11:43 ; — desirable, choice things i.e. garments Gen 27:15 (|| בגדים ); compare Dan 11:38 (|| יקרה אבן ), 11:43 ( מִצְרַיִם חֲמֻדוֺת ); = precious things Ezra 8:27 (as gold); ח ׳כלי 2Chr 20:25 ; ח ׳לֶחֶם Deut 10:3 ; of man only ׳אִישׁחֿ Dan 10:11 , 19 , and, without ׳ח אָ֫תָּה אישׁ, 9:23 thou art a precious treasure (on construction see Dr § 189, 2 ; see Bev and compare negative חמד Isa 53:2 ).
